subject: Observability activation: telemetry, dashboards & alert taxonomy for SummitHealth
body:
From: Alex Chu <alex.chu@summithealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Natalie Ortiz <natalie@consultedpartners.com>
Date: 2025-08-18 09:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability activation: telemetry, dashboards & alert taxonomy for SummitHealth

Hi Rafael —

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. We want to be sure the telemetry handoff is as lightweight as possible; key priorities for SummitHealth are: 1) service-level dashboards for latency & error rate, 2) tracing hooks for cross-service request IDs, and 3) an alert taxonomy that avoids paging on noisy, non-actionable signals.

Two quick asks before the kickoff: can you share a concise list of the dashboard widgets you recommend (top 6)? Also, do you have a suggested SLA-based alerting threshold matrix we can review?

Alex
Senior Engineer, Platform
SummitHealth

---
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Alex Chu <alex.chu@summithealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, Natalie Ortiz <natalie@consultedpartners.com>
Date: 2025-08-18 11:04 -0700
Subject: Observability activation: telemetry, dashboards & alert taxonomy for SummitHealth

Alex — thanks for the priorities and for the clear list. Looping in Ben (ops playbook lead), Laura (dashboard owner), and Monica (CS implementation) so we can align on a tight activation runbook.

Short plan (high level):
- Day 0: Kickoff call with SummitHealth + runbook walk-through (we suggest 45 minutes)
- Days 1–3: Tracing hook stubs + KV conventions implemented by SummitHealth (we provide examples)
- Days 4–7: Dashboard gallery import + basic panels (latency P50/P95, error rate, request volume, tail latency heatmap, capacity headroom, user-facing SLOs)
- Days 8–14: Alert taxonomy and escalation playbook; canary alerts enabled and tuned in staging

Attachments: I uploaded an initial draft of the alerting runbook, dashboard links, and a tracing hook spec spreadsheet to the shared Drive (links below). Please review the dashboard widgets list and the suggested threshold matrix; we can iterate on the kickoff.

Kickoff availability: I can do 2025-08-20 between 10:00–13:00 PT or 2025-08-21 08:00–11:00 PT. What works best for your SREs?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com

Attachments: RB-Alerting-Runbook-v0.9.pdf (PDF, 220KB); dashboards-collection-links.md (text); tracing-hook-specs.xlsx (spreadsheet)

---
From: Alex Chu <alex.chu@summithealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Natalie Ortiz <natalie@consultedpartners.com>
Date: 2025-08-18 13:27 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability activation: telemetry, dashboards & alert taxonomy for SummitHealth

Rafael —

Thanks. 2025-08-20 at 10:30 PT works; I’ll bring our SRE leads (names to follow). Quick clarification on the "tracing hook stubs + KV conventions" line — do you provide example middleware code for our platform (we run a mix of Go services + some Python workers)? If so, that would be great.

Also, the dashboard widget list you shared looks good as a starting point. My SREs will confirm thresholds after the first day of load testing.

Alex

---
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, Alex Chu <alex.chu@summithealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-20 10:49 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability activation: telemetry, dashboards & alert taxonomy for SummitHealth

Alex / Team —

Thanks for confirming the kickoff. A few practical notes from the ops side before the call:

- Middleware snippets: we have lightweight examples for Go (gin + net/http) and Python (FastAPI) that demonstrate request-id propagation and KV cache tagging. I’ll paste short snippets on the call and follow up with a GitHub gist.
- Dashboard import: Laura will share a dashboard bundle you can import into your Grafana/Looker instance; it contains parameterized panels so you can swap in your service names.
- Alert taxonomy: our recommended pattern is to classify alerts as SEV1/SEV2/SEV3 where SEV1 is user-impacting SLO breaches, SEV2 is sustained latency regressions, and SEV3 covers internal operational noise. We provide escalation steps for each.

Pre-read links: https://redwood-inference.app/drive/SH-telemetry-kickoff (runbook + examples)
DocuSign (onboarding MSA & data processing addendum): https://docusign.net/summithealth-onboarding-2025

I’ll join the 10:30 PT slot — see you on the kickoff.

-Ben Carter
Operational Playbooks, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

> On 2025-08-20 10:04 -0700, rafael_mendes@redwood.com wrote:
> Alex — just confirming we’re set for 10:30 PT and sending a short agenda for the 45-minute kickoff:
> 1) Introductions & goals (5m)
> 2) Tracing hook conventions & example deployment (10m)
> 3) Dashboard gallery & import demo (10m)
> 4) Alert taxonomy & escalation flow (10m)
> 5) Next steps & ownership (10m)
>
> Please flag anything you want added to the agenda.

---
From: Natalie Ortiz <natalie@consultedpartners.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, Alex Chu <alex.chu@summithealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-22 16:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability activation: telemetry, dashboards & alert taxonomy for SummitHealth

Thanks for the session today — that was very useful. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

1) Can you confirm the owner for runbook updates after we complete cutover? We’d like a single point of contact for edits and versioning.
2) We found one panel that needs a small filter tweak (service name wildcard); Laura, can you share the updated JSON for the panel?
3) Scheduling: SummitHealth preferred a phased cutover — enable dashboards & tracing in prod with passive alerts for 72 hours, then flip to active paging if stability looks good. We’ll capture that as part of the mutual rollout plan.

Proposed owner model: Redwood provides the runbook template and initial edits; SummitHealth owns site-specific content post-cutover. Rafael — can you confirm? If that matches, we’ll add a short ownership section to the runbook and sign off.

Best,
Natalie Ortiz
Principal Implementation Consultant
Consulted Partners

"""
